summary_text: Cycle-2j combined cycle-2i greeting re-enable + cycle-2j reference-voice bench executor complete. Phase 0 re-enabled the cycle-2i greeting drop-in (PRISM42_ENABLE_911_GREETING=1) cleanly; worker active and registered with LiveKit Cloud (region Germany 2). Phase 1 applied J0's 3-site patch to fish_speech_tts.py: env reads (DEFAULT_REFERENCE_AUDIO_PATH, DEFAULT_REFERENCE_AUDIO_TEXT), dataclass fields (reference_audio_path, reference_audio_text), and inline references_payload assembly with mutex guard against reference_id (engine drops references silently when both set; adapter mirrors that). Patch is ~50 LOC including comments, no new imports, py_compile clean. Phase 2 staged 2 LibriTTS WAVs at /opt/prism42/voice-refs/{wav1,wav2}.wav (md5 d08ca432... and ddfbc520...). Phase 3 ran 5 phrases x 3 conditions = 15 synth calls direct against Fish HTTP /v1/tts on the pod, all 15 succeeded with valid PCM. Latency: TTFB p95 5ms baseline -> 6ms WAV1/WAV2 (1ms absolute, 20% relative on already-instant streaming). Total render p95 1352ms baseline -> 1162ms WAV1 (-14.1%) -> 1250ms WAV2 (-7.5%) — both WAV conditions actually rendered FASTER than baseline. Peak amplitude tightened from baseline range [28006, 31088] to a uniform 28006 under both WAV conditions, consistent with reference-voice clipping the loudness envelope to the reference's distribution. No clipping, no silence, no truncation in any of 15 outputs. Audio specs all sane (44.1 kHz mono 16-bit PCM, durations 0.79-3.58 s, RMS 1453-9902). Decision is PARTIAL because the agent has no audio perception and cannot independently rate naturalness — metrics show no regression, both WAVs are tied for latency-improvement and tighter dynamic range, but only human listening can confirm 'sounds more like a calm dispatcher.' Adapter is patched and ready; no systemd drop-in installed (default off). User listens to listening_checklist.md and either installs 60-cycle2j-refvoice.conf with the chosen WAV path or accepts PARTIAL_KEEP_OFF.

rollback_instructions: 1. cycle-2j drop-in remove (only relevant if user later installs it): sudo rm /etc/systemd/system/prism42-worker.service.d/60-cycle2j-refvoice.conf && sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart prism42-worker
2. cycle-2i drop-in remove (separate): sudo rm /etc/systemd/system/prism42-worker.service.d/50-cycle2i-greeting.conf && sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart prism42-worker

3. fish_speech_tts.py file restore: ssh prism-mla-b300-h4h5 'sudo cp /opt/prism42/agents/livekit/fish_speech_tts.py.pre-cycle2j /opt/prism42/agents/livekit/fish_speech_tts.py && sudo systemctl restart prism42-worker'
4. Local file revert: git checkout agents/livekit/fish_speech_tts.py (changes are uncommitted; integrator commits or discards)
Time-to-recover: ~60-90s for full undo (single-file revert + systemd restart).
next_step_recommendation: User listens to audio/baseline/p1.wav vs audio/wav1/p1.wav vs audio/wav2/p1.wav (the 911 identity line — highest-stakes utterance) first. If a clear winner emerges, P2-P5 confirms consistency. Verdict path: PICK_WAV[1|2] -> install 60-cycle2j-refvoice.conf with that WAV's path + transcript -> restart worker -> confirm fish.reference_voice.loaded event fires. REJECT_BOTH or PARTIAL_KEEP_OFF -> no further action; baseline voice continues.
